  • Strong storytelling and positioning skills; able to simplify complexity for a non-expert audience
  • Comfortable directing AI tools to increase personal output and productivity
  • Ready to operate as an individual contributor now, with the ability to build and lead a team over time

Please note that at this time, we do not sponsor visas or transfers for new hires. Voltus teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location (in the US or Canada, unless otherwise indicated on the role description).

jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups and 1.2M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, the fastest-growing company in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

Engine is looking for a Director, Lodging Partner Acquisition to source, structure, and close net-new lodging supply partnerships that expand the rate content, coverage, and economics available on the Engine platform.

This is a full-cycle hunter role. You will identify and win new supply partners across supply aggregators and distribution partners, property management groups (PMGs), hotel chains, and large independent and complex properties — including casinos, resorts, and destination properties.

You’ll acquire supply across Engine’s growing set of booking products and distribution surfaces — spanning transient, group, and API-based channels (including Groups and Omni) — matching partners to where they fit best. Each is a distinct surface with its own content, and part of your role is structuring agreements that fit how each partner can best participate.

You will own each opportunity from first conversation through signed, activated agreement: building the pipeline, engaging supplier executives, structuring the commercial deal, and driving it live in partnership with our connectivity, onboarding, product, and Partner Success teams. Once a partner is signed and activated, you hand off ongoing account management and growth to Partner Success and move to the next target.

What You’ll Do

  • Own net-new supply acquisition end to end: source, qualify, negotiate, close, and drive to activation new lodging supply partnerships across aggregators and distribution partners, PMGs, chains, and large or complex independent properties.
  • Acquire supply across Engine’s surfaces: win supply for the core transient platform, Groups, and Omni (API), treating each as a distinct surface with its own content and structuring agreements accordingly.
  • Build and manage a supply pipeline: develop a named target list across supply categories and Engine product lines, tier opportunities by rate-content and net-direct-revenue potential, and self-source with creativity and urgency.
  • Lead executive-level deal-making: run complex, multi-stakeholder negotiations with commercial, revenue-management, and distribution leaders at supplier organizations, structuring agreements (direct rates, commissions/overrides, net-rate/contracted content, connectivity terms) that are commercially sound and durable.
  • Build commercial and distribution fluency: develop a strong working command of lodging distribution economics, rate/content models, connectivity paths, and supplier incentives, and use it to identify where Engine can unlock differentiated content.
  • Drive deals to activation, not just signature: partner with Connectivity, Onboarding, Product, and Finance to ensure signed agreements go live and produce consumed net direct revenue, then hand off cleanly to Partner Success.
  • Represent Engine in market: carry Engine’s supply story at industry events and executive forums, building credibility and relationships across the lodging ecosystem.
  • Maintain pipeline rigor: keep an accurate, well-organized pipeline and forecast, and communicate progress and risks clearly to leadership.

What You’ll Bring

  • 8+ years in business development, commercial partnerships, or enterprise/strategic sales, with a demonstrated focus on winning net-new business — not managing an inherited book.
  • A proven hunter track record: sourcing, structuring, and closing complex, high-value commercial agreements at meaningful scale. You find the opportunity, build the relationship, and drive it to signed.
  • Executive presence and negotiation strength: credibility with senior stakeholders and the ability to lead complex, multi-stakeholder negotiations to a durable close.
  • Commercial acumen: able to model and defend deal economics, structure creative terms, and align cross-functional partners on terms and execution.
  • A builder’s mindset: comfort creating the playbook, operating without a defined script, and turning ambiguity into signed, activated deals.
  • Fast learner with commercial curiosity: able to get up to speed quickly on lodging distribution and supplier economics (rate and content models, commissions/overrides, connectivity), even if you haven’t worked in them before.
  • Bonus: experience in travel, hospitality, lodging, marketplaces, or other supply/distribution businesses, and existing relationships across chains, PMGs, property groups, or distribution partners.

We accept applications for this role on an ongoing basis. We review applications as they are received and encourage interested candidates to apply early.

Applications for this role will be accepted through November 10, 2026 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation
Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, total compensation may include equity and/or variable pay (OTE). Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range
$164,000—$205,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & CompensationWe believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

  • Compensation: Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with opportunities for bonuses, commissions, and equity.
  • Benefits: Check out our full list at.
  • Environments for Success: Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we’ll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more.

Ready to Build the Future of Work Travel?Join us on our mission to transform how work travel works—for businesses, for travelers, and for the industry. Apply now and let’s make travel simpler, smarter, and more enjoyable—together.

jobs.description:
Job Summary:

Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director of Financial Planning and Analysis is responsible for the financial management, budgeting, and strategy of the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Leading a team of 3 financial analysts, the Director is responsible for the development of the School’s $400M+ annual operating budget, multi-year financial plan, monthly forecasts, and management reporting, as well as frequent ad hoc analyses.

A key member of the Office of Financial Services leadership team, the Director partners closely with the CFO, and regularly engages with administrative and departmental leaders across the Chan School. The Director plays a critical role in shaping the School’s financial strategy, providing actionable insights to inform resource allocation, investments, and long-range planning in support of the research and teaching mission.

This role is highly visible and requires the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, compelling narratives for a range of audiences, including the Dean, Executive Dean for Administration, and other School and University leaders.

Job-Specific Responsibilities:

Please Note: Applicants must have significant experience in sponsored research finance within a complex higher education, hospital, healthcare, or academic medical center environment, with higher education experience strongly preferred. This experience should be clearly demonstrated in the candidate’s resume and application materials in order to be formally considered for the position.

Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Strategic Financial Planning, Analysis, and Presentation
    • Direct and oversee all aspects of the School’s annual budget process; develop guidance and materials, analyze submissions, lead departmental meetings, and create a wholistic plan that aligns with School and University priorities and long-term financial sustainability
    • Build and refine the School’s multi-year financial plan, incorporating assumptions and modeling scenarios across a wide range of financial metrics; synthesize data into presentations and recommendations
    • Oversee the creation and continuous improvement of management reporting for the CFO, School leadership, and University stakeholders
    • Lead the development of monthly forecasts to proactively identify financial risks and opportunities; regularly provide ad hoc analysis in support of strategic decision making
    • Leveraging data from numerous sources, analyze monthly and year-end financial results and evaluate key drivers and trends
    • Design and frequently present financial materials, tailoring communication to financial and non-financial audiences across the School
  • Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement
    • Lead or contribute to special projects and strategic initiatives, often in collaboration with other finance and administrative colleagues; identify opportunities to streamline and enhance budgeting, forecasting, and reporting efforts
    • Serve as key liaison to departments, providing guidance on budgeting and financial analysis; work closely with leaders from Facilities and IT to ensure long-term capital and technology plans align with financial plans
    • Serve as key liaison to the University’s finance team; collaborate with FP&A Directors from all Harvard Schools in monthly meetings; represent the School in University-wide initiatives
  • Team Leadership and Management
    • Provide effective leadership and direct management of a team of three financial analysts
    • Foster a collaborative and innovative work environment that supports professional development, accountability, and continuous learning

PLEASE NOTE: This is a primarily remote position, however, scheduling flexibility may be required to come into the office for various meetings and events.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience required
  • Minimum of 10 years’ relevant work experience
  • 7+ years of experience in sponsored research finance within a complex higher education, hospital, healthcare, or academic medical center environment required; higher education experience strongly preferred
  • Supervisory experience required

Additional Qualifications and Skills:

  • Master's Degree in a related field is a plus
  • Demonstrated experience leading strategic financial planning and modeling within a large, decentralized organization, preferably in higher education, healthcare, research, or other mission-driven environments
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to synthesize complex financial information into clear communications and recommendations for senior leadership and non-financial stakeholders
  • Proven ability to manage competing priorities and navigate ambiguity in an evolving environment while maintaining attention to detail and accuracy
  • Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing high-performing analytical teams with a collaborative and service-oriented approach
  • Experience developing and improving financial reporting, dashboards, and analytical tools to support decision making and operational transparency
  • Advanced proficiency in financial systems and data analysis/presentation tools (e.g., Excel modeling, ERP systems, PowerPoint, etc.)
  • Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective partnerships across multiple financial and administrative areas
  • Knowledge of or experience with university budgeting models, sponsored research environments, endowment-funded institutions, or capital planning processes is a plus
  • Standard Hours/Schedule: 35 hours per week
  • Visa Sponsorship Information: Harvard University is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position
  • Pre-Employment Screening: Identity, Education, Criminal, Credit

Join the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health to support our mission of health research and education, and to be a part of the oldest institution of higher learning in the country!

  • The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health does not provide visa sponsorship, now or in the future, for staff positions.
  • Harvard University requires pre-employment reference checks and background screenings.
  • This position has a 180 day orientation and review period.

The health of our workforce is a priority for Harvard University. With that in mind, we strongly encourage all employees to be up to date on CDC-recommended vaccines.

Work Format Details

This position has been determined by school or unit leaders that the duties and responsibilities can effectively be performed fully remotely at a non-Harvard location. Employees in fully remote positions must work all scheduled hours in a Harvard registered state in compliance with the University’s Policy on Employment Outside of Massachusetts. At the discretion of the department, fully remote employees may occasionally be required on site at a Harvard location. Certain visa types and funding sources may limit work location. Individuals must meet work location sponsorship requirements prior to employment.

Salary Grade and Ranges

This position is salary grade level 060. Please visit  Harvard's Salary Ranges  to view the corresponding salary range and related information.

Benefits

Harvard offers a comprehensive benefits package that is designed to support a healthy work-life balance and your physical, mental and financial wellbeing. Because here, you are what matters. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Generous paid time off including parental leave
  • Medical, dental, and vision health insurance coverage starting on day one
  • Retirement plans with university contributions
  • Wellbeing and mental health resources
  • Support for families and caregivers
  • Professional development opportunities including tuition assistance and reimbursement
  • Commuter benefits, discounts and campus perks

Learn more about these and additional benefits on our Benefits & Wellbeing Page.

EEO/Non-Discrimination Commitment Statement

Harvard University is committed to equal opportunity and non-discrimination. We seek talent from all parts of society and the world, and we strive to ensure everyone at Harvard thrives. Our differences help our community advance Harvard's academic purposes.

Harvard has an equal employment opportunity policy that outlines our commitment to prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, religion, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law or identified in the university's non-discrimination policy. Harvard's equal employment opportunity policy and non-discrimination policy help all community members participate fully in work and campus life free from harassment and discrimination.

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

Why join the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health?

The Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is a world-renowned institution dedicated to advancing public health through cutting-edge research, education, and global collaboration. Our school is a special place to work because of its vibrant, mission-driven community, interdisciplinary approach, and commitment to addressing some of the most pressing health challenges worldwide. We foster a collaborative and inclusive work environment where innovation, continuous learning, and work-life balance are valued.

Learn more about the School’s mission, objectives, and core values, our Principles of Citizenship, and about the Dean’s AAA vision about our school’s ongoing strategic initiatives.

jobs.excerpt: The EVERSANA Medical Science Liaison/Senior Medical Science Liaison functions as a highly trained, field-based, scientific expert in ophthalmology, particularly retinal disease, who engages health care professionals and leaders in clinical, scientific, value-based care and research-based peer to peer scientific exchange around our client’s product.
jobs.description:
The EVERSANA Medical Science Liaison/Senior Medical Science Liaison functions as a highly trained, field-based, scientific expert in ophthalmology, particularly retinal disease, who engages health care professionals and leaders in clinical, scientific, value-based care and research-based peer to peer scientific exchange around our client’s product.

Following regulatory and corporate guidelines, they will facilitate and build scientific relationships and collaborations with scientific communities. This position interacts with local, regional, and national Key Opinion Leaders (KOLs) and health care practitioners (HCPs), as well as professional societies and organizations. The MSL will need to be fully engaged with pertinent professional societies, as well as other value-based institutions and associations including ophthalmology and optometry clinics and retinal specialists that are involved with the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD). The MSL will be the field based scientific expert regarding our client’s product.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Function as the primary medical point of contact in geographic area.
  • Maintain clinical and scientific expertise in ophthalmology with specific focus in standards of care related to the treatment of neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD), commonly known as wet AMD.
  • Engage in well informed, compliant, robust, and accurate scientific peer exchange around the treatment of wet AMD, and the science our client’s product.
  • Engage in medical & scientific exchange with the medical/scientific community including advisory boards.
  • Conduct pre-launch KOL profiling efforts to enhance depth of product/disease/scientific knowledge. Facilitate top account/institution profiling efforts to enhance understanding of patient care pathways, including treatment protocol development and novel therapies.
  • Develop and track Strategic KOL engagement plans - identify, develop, and maintain long-term collaborative relationships with KOLs within assigned region.
  • Support health systems, population health leaders, and medical quality professionals by offering clinical, public health, medical quality, and other scientific information to help guide medical decisions
  • Deliver clinical and scientific presentations to healthcare providers, health systems, and medical group leadership, as well as community/advocacy groups.
  • Build relationships and assist in the development of key opinion leaders.
  • Build relationships with key decision makers in health systems, medical groups, healthcare provider offices, state departments of public health, advocacy organizations, and national/regional professional societies.
  • Provide insight into market trends and clinical intelligence.
  • Collaborates with the Medical Affairs leadership in the development of key opinion leaders.
  • Collaborate with clients and thought leaders on a national, regional, and local level to develop clinical insights that support medical research associated with new and existing products.
  • Supports implementation team as needed.
  • Identify, attend and report on local/regional educational events such as national symposia and scientific/clinical meetings and CME events.
  • Manage time and travel expense budget for scientific exchange and clinical education activities within dedicated regions.
  • Demonstrate excellent written and oral communication skills, as well as effective presentation skills
  • Ability to work well independently and manage time effectively.
  • Strong attention to detail with a focus on producing high-quality work.
  • Strong verbal and written communication; public speaking skills.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Uphold company mission and values through accountability, innovation, integrity, quality, and teamwork.
  • Support and comply with the company’s Quality Management System policies and procedures
  • Responsible for all clinical program requests and for unsolicited requests for information.
  • May collaborate with R&D Team to support sites and investigators participating in the company-sponsored clinical trials.
  • Work collaboratively and compliantly with commercial colleagues to assure product strategic imperatives are represented cross functionally in account engagement.
  • Respond to and document unsolicited requests for information on clinical initiatives.
  • May serve as a resource for investigator-initiated trial (IIT) proposals.
  • Provide internal teams with feedback and insights from interactions with KOLs.
  • Represent our client at medical meetings through Medical Affairs Scientific Booth coverage and other related activities.
  • Attend congresses as appropriate and develop meaningful internal reports of the congresses covered.
  • Adhere to corporate SOPs and ensure vigilant compliance with relevant legal and regulatory guidelines governing scientific interactions with physicians and healthcare professionals across all activities, including those related to clinical trials, scientific interactions with internal and external groups, and responses to unsolicited requests for medical/scientific information.
  • Consistently demonstrate a high standard of excellence in the management of assigned territory while also contributing to the success of colleagues and the MSL team.
  • Willingness to contribute to the achievement of organizational goals beyond the borders of a geographic territory.
  • Be solidly versed in the clinical data such that the full range of innovative science, clinical, outcome, economic and value aspects of our client’s products can be appreciated by the healthcare practitioner, formulary member or payer.
  • Provide medical support, clinical input, and/or training for internal teams as requested.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • An advanced degree (e.g., OD, PharmD, PhD, MD, MSN, DNP, or NP/PA) is required.
  • MSL: A minimum of 2 years previous MSL experience necessary with a minimum of 1 year in ophthalmology with working knowledge of retinal disorders.
  • Sr. MSL: A minimum of 5 years of pharma experience and 3 years of rare disease, ophthalmology experience.
  • Prior product launch experience desired.
  • Exhibits the highest level of scientific, business, and clinical acumen with excellent communication and networking skills.
  • The ability to interpret and present scientific data to engage KOLs.
  • Working knowledge of standards of care for prostate cancer required.
  • Previous experience sharing scientific content with payer systems is highly desirable.
  • Working knowledge of Ophthalmology screening and wellness programs is strongly desired.
  • Ability to present complex scientific and value and evidence data to payors and/or formulary committees is required.
  • Working knowledge of institutions and clinics in selected geographies is expected.
  • Excellent written and oral presentation skills.
  • Ability to travel frequently (70%) with overnight stays (e.g., KOL meetings, site locations, internal meetings, medical meetings and congresses, training).

Embrace Diversity I create an environment of awareness and respect.

jobs.title: Senior / Lead Analyst, Customer Insights
jobs.excerpt: Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all.
jobs.description:
Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We believe that there is a better healthcare world – one powered by data. Our platform transforms complex, diverse data into a unified foundation for health, helping organizations deliver better care, boost revenue, and lower costs.
We’re a team of fiercely driven individuals committed to making healthcare more sustainable—and we’re looking for passionate people to help us get there.
For more information, visit .

Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia

Analytics sits at the center of how Arcadia turns complex healthcare data into better outcomes and smarter decisions.

On the product side, that means building and owning the productized analytics engines — risk, medical economics, episodes-of-care, and more — that power Arcadia's platform company-wide, built once and delivered at scale across our entire customer base.

On the Customer Insights side, that means going deep on a specific customer's specific problem: custom data models, bespoke dashboards, advisory work, and long-running embedded programs that don't fit a one-size-fits-all product. We describe Customer Insights' work as sitting between a platform and a plan — more customized and hands-on than an off-the-shelf reporting product, more flexible and embedded in the customer's actual decisions than a traditional outsourced consulting engagement.

We're currently hiring for several closely related analyst roles across this broader Analytics organization — spanning ownership of one of Arcadia's core analytics engines, program-specific analytical development for a major state Medicaid risk-stratification initiative, versatile project and retainer delivery across our health system and payer customers, and dedicated analytics support for a major national health plan's Medicaid program. All of these roles sit at the Senior Analyst or Lead Analyst level, combine technical excellence with real influence over analytic strategy and (for some placements) product direction, and shape how Arcadia and its customers use data to improve population health outcomes, reduce costs, and enable smarter healthcare decisions.

The skills and experience below are characteristic across these roles as a set — not every requirement applies to every specific seat, and we don't expect any one candidate to bring all of it. We'll work with you during the interview process to identify which role is the best fit for your background and interests.

What Success Looks Like

In 3 months

  • Ramp into your specific engagement's data model, technical stack, and stakeholder relationships — every Customer Insights engagement has real history and context to build into, not a blank slate
  • Learn Arcadia's core analytics platform and toolset (QuickSight, Foundry, dbt, the AWS ecosystem) as used in your engagement
  • Deliver your first piece of analytical work that demonstrates clear value to your engagement's stakeholders

In 6 months

  • Own meaningful pieces of delivery independently — whether that's a program's analytical development, a portfolio of retainer/project work, or a dedicated account's dashboarding and reporting
  • Be a credible, independent presence in front of the customers or partners tied to your engagement
  • Contribute to at least one reusable analytical asset, framework, or automation that extends beyond your immediate engagement
  • Begin taking on the ongoing health of your area, not just its delivery — standing up a backlog/tech-debt process, or growing into a broader backup role alongside your engagement's primary owner, depending on placement

In 12 months

  • Be a recognized expert in your engagement area, trusted with its most complex or ambiguous work
  • Actively identify and pursue opportunities for automation, scalability, and reuse across your work
  • Have grown into deeper ownership than where you started — full backup or co-owner on an account, sole steward of a program's tech-debt and backlog, or, for analytics-engine placements, the architect shaping that engine's roadmap toward being market-leading

What You'll Be Doing

    Technical Analytical Delivery

  • Translate ambiguous or partially-scoped business and clinical questions into a concrete, buildable data plan, then build the underlying data model, code, and analysis on top of it
  • Develop and maintain analytical pipelines and reusable data assets using SQL, dbt, and Arcadia's core data platform (Foundry, AWS data lake environments)
  • For analytics-engine placements: serve as the lead analytics strategist for at least one of Arcadia's productized analytics engines (e.g., risk, medical economics, episodes-of-care), owning it end-to-end while contributing to others
  • For engagements involving predictive or risk models: design and build the models, partnering with a dedicated Data Science team on training and validation — a consultative relationship, not a daily modeling partnership
  • Build dashboards, provider scorecards, registries, and other analytical deliverables (QuickSight and beyond) on top of that modeling work, as the engagement calls for it
  • Maintain the analytical integrity and quality of your work, flagging issues before they reach a customer or partner; for senior placements, oversee analytic quality standards and rigor across engagements more broadly, not just your own

    • Program and Project Management

  • Manage delivery — whether that's a single program's delivery calendar and decision log, or a portfolio of concurrent projects across multiple customers — surfacing risks and tradeoffs before they become blocking issues
  • Create client-facing materials — status decks, decision memos, technical explainers — tailored to a range of stakeholders, from highly technical counterparts to policy or business stakeholders with limited technical background
  • Delegate routine or repeatable work to junior analysts as your engagement grows, and help cross-train others for coverage
  • Lead cross-functional analytic initiatives that span multiple teams or engagements

    • Customer and Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as a primary or supporting day-to-day contact for your engagement's customers or delivery partners, navigating scope and timeline conversations directly
  • Partner with Customer Management, Growth, Product, and/or Engineering — depending on placement — on account strategy, product direction, or analytics roadmap; for analytics-engine placements, partner closely with product and engineering to deliver Arcadia's analytics roadmap and contribute directly to product innovation
  • Hold real authority at the boundaries where your work meets someone else's — able to require rework or hold a handoff that isn't ready (e.g., with a partner Data Science team), or push back on what's actually worth building with Customer Management, Growth, or Product, rather than defaulting to whatever's asked
  • Act as an internal thought leader on your area of expertise, contributing to Arcadia's broader analytics strategy and reusable methodology — and, for some placements, an external one, representing Arcadia's analytic capabilities at customer meetings, industry conferences, and in publications

    • Team Contribution

  • Mentor and develop junior analysts, building organizational capacity beyond your own individual delivery
  • Take ownership of your area's long-term health, not just its immediate delivery — a backlog/tech-debt log, a growing backup role on an account, or a roadmap for an analytics engine, depending on placement
  • Apply AI tooling as a standard part of your workflow — analysis, QA, documentation — not an occasional accelerant
  • Identify opportunities for automation, scalability, and reusability in analytical delivery, and help build those improvements out

What You'll Bring

  • Strong SQL and data modeling expertise — able to translate ambiguous business or clinical requirements into a concrete data plan, then build the underlying code and analysis on top of it
  • Healthcare data experience — claims and/or clinical data, with value-based care familiarity
  • Direct customer- or partner-facing experience — comfortable scoping and presenting without close oversight
  • Comfortable adopting AI tooling as a standard part of an analytical workflow
  • For Lead-level placement: demonstrated experience leading analytical work independently, managing multiple stakeholders, and mentoring less experienced analysts

    • Note: our experience bar across these roles generally skews toward Lead-level expectations, even for some Senior Analyst placements — but not every skill listed here or below applies to every specific seat.

Would Love For You To Have

  • Experience with dbt-based analytics engine development (e.g., risk, medical economics, episodes-of-care) and partnering with product/engineering on roadmap
  • Dashboarding experience — QuickSight or a comparable BI tool
  • Enough quantitative/ML fluency to build models and hand them to a Data Science team for training
  • Experience with medical economics, risk algorithms, quality data, and/or episodes-of-care analytics
  • Prior experience with state Medicaid programs or similar large government health programs
  • Prior experience in a project-based/retainer delivery model spanning multiple customers, rather than a single dedicated account
  • Experience working within a prime contractor or partner structure on shared delivery
  • Experience presenting analytic capabilities externally — customer meetings, industry conferences, publications
  • Python for analysis and QA; familiarity with the AWS ecosystem, Jira, and Confluence

    • Note: this list spans skills relevant to several different roles across the Analytics organization — we don't expect any given candidate to have all of them. Bring what you have; we'll talk through the rest during the interview process.

What You'll Get

  • Become a member of the talented, energized, diverse and purpose-driven Arcadian Community with decades of collective experience in population health, product development, and data science
  • Employee driven programs and initiatives for personal and professional development
  • A flexible, remote-friendly company with personality and heart
  • Competitive compensation and strong benefits, including Flexible Time Off

    • The opportunity to:

  • Own real, high-stakes analytical work across some of Arcadia's most complex customer relationships and highest-visibility internal analytics products
  • Work across a genuinely varied set of problems — deep technical program ownership, versatile multi-account delivery, or company-wide analytics engines, depending on placement
  • Build models and analytical assets that directly shape care and coverage decisions for the members and patients they serve

    • Senior Analyst: $125,000 – $145,000 a year

    Lead Analyst: $145,000 – $170,000 a year

About Arcadia

Arcadia.io helps innovative providers and payers across the country transform healthcare to reduce cost while improving patient health. We do this by aggregating large amounts of disparate data, applying algorithms to identify opportunities to provide better patient care, and making those opportunities actionable by physicians at the point of care in near-real time. We are passionate about helping our customers drive meaningful outcomes. We are growing fast and have emerged as a market leader in the highly competitive population health management software market and have been recognized by industry analysts KLAS, IDC, Forrester, and Chilmark for our leadership. For a better sense of our brand and products, please explore our website.

Protect Yourself

If you have concerns about the authenticity of a job offer or recruitment-related communication claiming to be from Arcadia, we encourage you to verify by contacting us directly at (781) 202-3600 and select option 3. For more information, visit our website.
This position is responsible for following all Security policies and procedures in order to protect all PHI under Arcadia's custodianship as well as Arcadia Intellectual Properties. For any security-specific roles, the responsibilities would be further defined by the hiring manager.

Hovercraft is a dynamic and innovative creative design firm that partners with brands to craft compelling experiences through design, strategy, and technology. This role will require travel to facilitate face-to-face client interactions and to oversee creative production in person when needed. The Senior Creative Producer will work closely with internal teams, clients, and external partners to ensure projects are delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest standards.

This is a leadership role, ideal for someone with significant experience in creative production, project management, and a passion for delivering exceptional design and creative outcomes. The ideal candidate is an excellent communicator, a natural collaborator, and has hands-on experience managing a variety of creative projects while staying on time, scope & budget. This role is for someone with an affinity for youth culture, fashion, sport, and design.

  • Project Management: Lead end-to-end project management for creative campaigns, design projects, digital experiences, and branding initiatives. Ensure seamless coordination and execution from inception to completion.

Arcadia is the most trusted healthcare platform powering outcomes. We transform complex healthcare data into trusted intelligence, helping providers, payers, and life sciences organizations act with clarity, make confident decisions, and achieve measurable clinical, operational, and financial outcomes.

Built on a comprehensive data foundation spanning tens of millions of patient lives, Arcadia combines advanced analytics and responsible AI to surface meaningful insights, coordinate action, and improve performance at scale. Our approach to AI and automation is governed and transparent — designed to strengthen human expertise, not replace judgment or obscure responsibility.

Hundreds of organizations rely on Arcadia to improve cost, quality, and outcomes. Backed by Nordic Capital, we continue to invest in our platform, AI capabilities, and people as we pursue our purpose: helping healthcare deliver better outcomes for every person, every community, and every generation.

Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia

Arcadia’s data and analytics platform is used by hundreds of health systems, ACOs, payers, and life sciences organizations, touching tens of millions of patient lives. This role owns how our agentic capabilities perform at that same scale: accurate, transparent about their own confidence, and safe for the clinicians, care teams, and patients who depend on them.

As a staff-level individual contributor, you will own the product-layer decisions that shape agent behavior, including prompting, retrieval and context, memory and state, evaluation, and escalation, while partnering with Product and Engineering on the systems that support them. Your work will help Arcadia make evidence-based launch decisions and scale responsible AI that is steerable, trustworthy, and ready for real healthcare workflows.

What Success Looks Like

In 3 months

  • You have established a production-grounded baseline for priority agentic workflows, with documented failure modes, severity-weighted evaluation rubrics, and a clear measurement plan
  • You have mapped the current retrieval, context, memory, and escalation patterns and identified the highest-value opportunities to improve reliability, calibration, and cost
  • You have earned trust across Product and Engineering by turning production evidence into clear, actionable recommendations

In 6 months

  • Production-representative evaluation suites and regression checks inform model-change decisions for priority agentic workflows
  • You have delivered measurable improvements in accuracy, reliability, steerability, latency, or cost for one or more priority workflows
  • Human-review and escalation behavior has been validated under adversarial and edge-case conditions, with decision criteria and ownership boundaries clearly documented

In 12 months

  • Arcadia has a repeatable product-layer AI performance practice that moves from production failure to diagnosis, experiment, evaluation, and release decision
  • High-severity regressions are caught earlier, and agent behavior is more transparent, calibrated, and trustworthy at scale
  • Model cards, intended-use guidance, limitations, and performance documentation are current and useful to product and customer-facing teams

What You'll Be Doing

  • Design and iterate on agent behavior across real, live workflows, including long-horizon, multi-turn agentic tasks
  • Design retrieval and context architecture so the right source data reaches a model in the right structure and agents remain grounded in real data rather than filling gaps with assumptions
  • Design memory and state handling across multi-turn and multi-agent flows, determining what is carried forward, summarized, or dropped and why
  • Create context and prompt templates that combine few-shot examples, structured formatting, and reasoning scaffolding for consistent agent behavior
  • Improve performance through prompting, tool-use strategy, and context construction, validated through direct experimentation rather than guesswork
  • Build and run evaluations against real production conditions to measure performance, regressions, failure modes, and edge cases
  • Author evaluation rubrics, quality heuristics, and thresholds that weight failures by severity and cost, not just frequency, and monitor those measures against production behavior
  • Design and validate escalation paths that route agents to human review based on confidence and uncertainty while preserving safety and consistency under adversarial and edge-case conditions
  • Design for cost-aware performance alongside latency, reliability, and accuracy through efficient context construction and tool-call economy
  • Evaluate and sign off on model changes by baselining current behavior, running comparative evaluations, and making the go/no-go call before a change reaches a customer
  • Maintain product-level AI documentation, including model cards, intended use, limitations, and known failure modes, so customer-facing teams work from actual agent behavior
  • Partner closely with Product and product managers to ensure agents are not just capable, but steerable, trustworthy, and ready to scale

What You'll Bring

  • We value equivalent practical experience that demonstrates the depth required for this staff-level role
  • 8+ years of production software engineering experience, including 3+ years of hands-on ownership of ML, LLM, or agentic systems in production, with direct experience in healthcare, finance, or another regulated industry
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose why an agent failed, correctly attribute the fix to instruction, retrieval, context, or memory design, and weigh failures by severity and cost rather than frequency alone
  • Hands-on experience with RAG architecture, production-grounded evaluation frameworks, and fallback or human-in-the-loop logic for automated systems
  • Working familiarity with AWS AI/ML services, including Bedrock and SageMaker, sufficient to build and evaluate effectively in Arcadia’s environment
  • Evidence-led judgment and the credibility to push back on launch decisions, paired with a builder’s instinct to run the experiment and move from a production failure to a fix

Would Love for You to Have

  • Experience applying AI to healthcare data or workflows where safety, transparency, and calibrated uncertainty directly affect care teams or patients
  • Experience with long-horizon, multi-turn or multi-agent workflows and product-level AI documentation such as model cards

What You'll Get

  • The opportunity to define how agent performance, safety, and readiness are measured for production healthcare workflows
  • Meaningful ownership across prompts, context, memory, evaluations, and escalation patterns at product scale
  • A cross-functional role translating production evidence into AI improvements used across Arcadia’s platform
  • A mission-driven company working to improve how patients receive care
  • A flexible, remote-friendly culture with personality and heart
  • Employee-driven programs and initiatives for personal and professional development
  • Membership in the talented, energized, diverse, and purpose-driven Arcadian community

About Arcadia

Arcadia.io helps innovative providers and payers across the country transform healthcare to reduce cost while improving patient health. We do this by aggregating large amounts of disparate data, applying algorithms to identify opportunities to provide better patient care, and making those opportunities actionable by physicians at the point of care in near-real time. We are passionate about helping our customers drive meaningful outcomes. We are growing fast and have emerged as a market leader in the highly competitive population health management software market and have been recognized by industry analysts KLAS, IDC, Forrester, and Chilmark for our leadership. For a better sense of our brand and products, please explore our website.

Protect Yourself

If you have concerns about the authenticity of a job offer or recruitment-related communication claiming to be from Arcadia, we encourage you to verify by contacting us directly at (781) 202-3600 and select option 3. For more information, visit our website.

jobs.title: Head of Revenue Operations
jobs.excerpt: Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all.
jobs.description:
Arcadia is dedicated to happier, healthier days for all. We believe that there is a better healthcare world — one powered by data. Our platform transforms complex, diverse data into a unified foundation for health, helping organizations deliver better care, boost revenue, and lower costs.

We're a team of fiercely driven individuals committed to making healthcare more sustainable — and we're looking for passionate people to help us get there.

For more information, visit arcadia.io.

Why This Role Is Important to Arcadia

Arcadia's commercial team depends on consistent process, clean pipeline data, and forecasts to help manage and grow the business. As a fast-growing company, we need to scale our infrastructure, systems and operating model to one that aligns to the pace of the growth. This role owns the systems, tools, and cadences that make pipeline reviews, forecasting, and reporting consistent and accurate across the entire commercial team.

Part of the initial mandate is understanding the current ecosystem of tools and technology that support commercial and revenue operations today, and making recommendations on the optimal tech stack for the function going forward — one that is AI native. This person will be the accountable owner of that stack and roadmap, partnering closely with Product and Tech to build the AI-native operating system rather than building it in isolation.

This person will run point on sales operations and the forecasting cadence, and will build the AI-powered operating layer (dashboards, briefings, and workflow tools) that gives the entire commercial organization — not just its leadership — real-time visibility and leverage.

This is role is for someone who is execution oriented. You'll work in the tools yourself — not just direct others to — while also setting the strategy, systems, and rigor that let Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance move as one aligned, predictable engine.

What Success Looks Like

In 3 months

What You'll Be Doing

  • Evaluate the current ecosystem of tools and technology supporting commercial and revenue operations, and make recommendations on the optimal, AI-native tech stack for the function
  • Serve as the accountable owner of that tech stack and roadmap, partnering closely with Product and Tech to build the AI-native operating system rather than building it in isolation
  • Own pricing strategy, SKUs, and the end-to-end quote-to-cash process, ensuring pricing structures and deal execution are clean, consistent, and scalable
  • Own the forecasting cadence and develop robust, repeatable forecasting models (pipeline, bookings, ARR) that improve accuracy and predictability
  • Build the AI-powered operating layer — automated briefings, pipeline intelligence, meeting prep, and reporting dashboards — that gives the commercial organization real-time visibility
  • Establish and maintain a unified KPI framework, ensuring alignment on definitions, visibility, and accountability across the funnel
  • Act as connective tissue across live opportunities, coordinating Marketing, Finance, the RFP team, Value Enablement, and Sales Engineering so they're effectively leveraged
  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and Finance leadership to align execution with company goals and financial plans
  • Analyze pipeline health, conversion rates, and sales efficiency to identify opportunities and drive improvements
  • Design and manage sales compensation and incentive plans that align with business objectives and drive desired behaviors across GTM teams

What You'll Bring

    The Role, Done Before

  • You have held this exact role — Head/Director of Revenue Operations or equivalent — at a company of similar growth stage, and can point to what you built and owned.

    • Growth-Stage Fluency

  • Track record of operating at growth-stage speed and ambiguity — scrappy, resourceful, and comfortable building infrastructure from scratch rather than administering something already built. Candidates whose experience is exclusively at large, mature organizations without growth-stage exposure are not a fit for this seat.

    • Deep SaaS Metrics Expertise

  • Strong command of key SaaS metrics including ARR, NDR, GDR, CAC, LTV, pipeline coverage, and sales productivity, and how they connect to business performance.

    • Forecasting & Modeling Rigor

  • Proven ability to build and operationalize forecasting models (e.g., pipeline velocity, ARR forecasting) that improve accuracy and predictability.

  • Deep, hands-on experience owning a CRM (Salesforce or equivalent) and the broader GTM tech stack — configuration, data integrity, and workflow design, not just consumption of dashboards.

Would Love for You to Have

  • Experience supporting a high-growth SaaS company through key milestones (e.g., post-acquisition integration, scale-up, or M&A)
  • Familiarity with modern BI, AI, and planning tools (e.g., Sigma, Adaptive, Salesforce ecosystem, AI-native reporting/agent tools) and building self-service analytics environments
  • Experience designing and optimizing sales compensation plans at scale

What You'll Get

  • The mandate to build a consistent, predictable commercial engine — including its AI-powered tooling — rather than inherit and maintain one
  • A growth path from individual contributor to leading the people and functions that support sales operations as Arcadia scales
  • A mission-driven culture where your work supports better healthcare outcomes

jobs.excerpt: Please note: We’re hiring across multiple locations in England, including Edinburgh, London, Yorkshire, Newcastle, Exeter, Cambridge, and more!
jobs.description:
Please note: We’re hiring across multiple locations in England, including Edinburgh, London, Yorkshire, Newcastle, Exeter, Cambridge, and more! To apply, you must have a valid UK driving licence, access to a car, and be willing to travel within your local area for appointments.

The Company

We’re Octopus Legacy: one of the fastest growing tech companies in the country, part of the UK’s most exciting and best-trusted group (you may have heard of some of our sister companies…) and we have a mission.

We’re on a path to scale, aiming to become a household name while transforming a long-established industry and helping our customers prepare for, and find support after, death.

But we can’t do it alone, and that’s why we’re assembling a team of top performers to build with us.

Ready to be part of something big?

The Role

We are seeking a dedicated Estate Planning Consultant who will be responsible for conducting home visits to assist clients in the process of drafting and creating wills. You will take the time to discuss your clients requirements in detail, explaining how the use of wills, trusts and lasting powers of attorney can work to protect them, their estate and their loved ones. The ideal candidate will excel in providing personalised and comprehensive guidance to individuals and families, ensuring their wishes are accurately documented whilst showing compassion and care.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Conduct in-depth consultations during home visits to understand clients' unique needs, assets, and preferences for estate planning
  • Guide clients through the legal aspects of will creation, addressing questions and concerns with clarity and expertise
  • Collaborate with legal teams and resources to stay informed about current estate planning laws and regulations
  • Maintain a meticulous record-keeping system to track client information, preferences, and any legal documentation
  • Support with online Wills and other services within the company when required
  • Provide exceptional customer service by offering ongoing support and addressing any post-visit inquiries or adjustments
  • Stay abreast of industry trends and best practices in estate planning to enhance service delivery

Who Are You?

  • Comfortable being fully remote on appointments (opportunity to be in office outside of appointments)
  • Must have a full UK driving license and be willing to drive around London
  • STEP qualified (preferred)
  • Knowledge of how to write Wills and understanding the legalities
  • Knowledge of how LPAs work
  • In-depth understanding of Octopus Legacy’s services and ability to upsell
  • Proficient in identifying indicators of concerns related to clients' testamentary capacity
  • High levels of empathy, discretion and care
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills
  • Active listening skills and the ability to understand the customer’s needs
  • Proactive in initiating tasks independently and effectively following instructions
  • Flexible schedule to accommodate home visits based on clients' availability

Our Mission

When people think about planning for death they think about wills, life insurance and funerals. We take these cold processes and turn them into something more human. Share more than money: leave voice notes, music, recipes. Shape a legacy that connects you while you're here. And after you're gone.

Founded by Sam after his mum died suddenly, we’re a group of people who work in death because we’ve been affected by it. We know the difference a good plan makes, and what it’s like when there isn’t one.

Death can come between us, leave mess, legal fees, frustration. But it can also make us stronger. We see a world where people talk openly about death, and work out the real meaning of legacy, one that connects to them. We’re here to make that world happen.

Benefits:

  • Octopus share incentive scheme.
  • Flexible holiday + extra day off for your Birthday.
  • Vitality Health & Life Insurance.
  • Pension scheme.
  • Enhanced parental leave.
  • Free Will & LPAs + discounts on other Octopus services.

You'll work in TypeScript across frontend and backend systems. You'll design the SDK's Node.js core and public application programming interface (API), and work in the clients that use it. You'll have senior and staff engineers alongside you to help with design. You'll own the implementation of scoped packages and ship improvements with minimal guidance while collaborating with the team on larger architectural changes.

Some examples of our projects:

  • The Duo Client SDK, extracting versioned, publishable packages from the GitLab Language Server
  • The GitLab Language Server, rebuilt on top of the SDK as our polyglot surface
  • Duo Chat on the web, as one of the SDK's first consumers

What you'll do

  • Develop secure, well-tested, and performant TypeScript features that solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity.
  • Ship small features and improvements with minimal guidance, writing tests with every merge request and contributing to code reviews and design discussions.
  • Extract and publish TypeScript packages from the GitLab Language Server, migrating consumers incrementally so no parallel implementation is left to drift.
  • Design durable public APIs with clear interfaces, semantic versioning, changelogs, and deprecation paths for external consumers.
  • Build isomorphic core packages that isolate platform-specific behavior in adapters at the edges.
  • Build and improve SDK client surfaces, including Vue 3 components in Duo Chat on the web, in collaboration with product, design, and engineering teams.
  • Strengthen credential handling across hosts, including bearer tokens, session cookies, and CSRF protection.
  • Optimize bundle size, startup cost, and dependency weight for browser consumers, and support a Tier 2 on-call rotation for urgent engineering issues.

What you'll bring

  • Understanding of the differences between running code in Node.js and in the browser, and how to write code that works in both.
  • A security-minded development approach, including careful credential handling and performance optimization.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely in writing about technical problems, propose iterative solutions, and work effectively in an agile environment.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Vice President of Engagement serves as the university’s primary external ambassador, responsible for building, mobilizing, and stewarding the relationships that enable institutional growth, influence, and long-term impact. This role is part of the Senior Leadership Team responsible for cultivating and stewarding the relationships that power the university’s mission, reputation, and long-term sustainability.

This role leads the design and execution of an integrated engagement strategy that brings together philanthropy, partnerships, marketing, impact, alumni and community engagement, and stakeholder stewardship into a unified function. The Vice President drives the university’s resource mobilization efforts, securing funding and strategic support to advance its mission, while cultivating partnerships that expand its reach, relevance, and contribution across Africa and the world.

Central to the role is the responsibility to build and sustain a powerful, lifelong community of students, alumni, parents, staff, donors, and partners; ensuring that engagement with the university is meaningful, consistent, and anchored in shared purpose.

The role also oversees the university’s marketing, branding, and public relations strategy, ensuring a clear, compelling, and differentiated institutional voice, and leads impact reporting and storytelling to demonstrate the university’s outcomes and influence to stakeholders.

Through strong external representation, relationship leadership, strategic communications, and institutional convening, the Vice President positions the university as a trusted partner, connector, and platform for advancing leadership and impact on the continent.

ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

Fundraising & Business Development

  • Designing and executing a comprehensive fundraising & business development strategy including major gifts, foundations, corporate giving, and development campaigns.
  • Building and managing relationships with high-net-worth individuals, philanthropic foundations, and institutional donors.
  • Partnering with leadership and the Board to identify and cultivate strategic donors.
  • Developing compelling funding propositions aligned with the university’s mission and programs.
  • Establishing systems for donor stewardship, reporting, and impact communication.
  • Leading major institutional fundraising campaigns when required.
  • Building the process, data and systems to ensure seamless coordination of the customer experience, and data collection

Strategic Partnerships & Ecosystem Development

  • Building long-term relationships with companies, foundations, governments, NGOs, and global institutions.
  • Structuring partnerships that create value across student opportunities, program development, funding, and thought leadership.
  • Identifying opportunities for collaboration that advance African leadership development, entrepreneurship and innovation.
  • Representing the university in key external forums and strategic alliances.

Alumni & Community Engagement

  • Leading the strategy for alumni engagement across the continent and globally.
  • Developing programs that strengthen relationships between the university and its alumni: students, parents, and staff community.
  • Creating meaningful engagement opportunities including mentorship, career support, investment networks, and community impact initiatives.
  • Building systems that ensure alumni and parents remain lifelong ambassadors and contributors to the university’s mission.

Stewardship & Relationship Management

  • Developing structured stewardship programs for donors, partners, and strategic supporters.
  • Designing relationship management systems to track and strengthen institutional relationships.
  • Strategically positioning senior leadership as credible thought leaders within key stakeholder relationships, expanding ALU's reach and influence across priority networks and sectors.
  • Overseeing communications and reporting that demonstrate the impact of stakeholder contributions.

Marketing, Brand, PR & Impact

  • Developing and executing an integrated marketing and brand strategy aligned with the university’s mission and growth priorities.
  • Overseeing public relations and media engagement, ensuring consistent, high-quality external communications and reputation management.
  • Shaping and safeguarding the university’s brand identity, voice, and positioning across all channels, assets and markets.
  • Leading impact reporting and storytelling, translating data and outcomes into compelling narratives for donors, partners, and the broader community.
  • Ensuring alignment between fundraising, partnerships, and communications, so that messaging effectively supports resource mobilization and stakeholder engagement.
  • Building systems and content that elevate the university’s profile as a thought leader and impact-driven institution in Africa and globally.

Events, Hosting and Org-Wide Hospitality

  • Leading the strategy for high-impact institutional events, summits, convenings, and leadership gatherings.
  • Ensuring the university hosts partners, donors, and dignitaries with exceptional hospitality and professionalism.
  • Designing events that strengthen relationships and elevate the university’s reputation.
  • Supporting flagship events including graduations, donor gatherings, signature ALU events and leadership forums.

External Relations

  • Representing the university with philanthropic, corporate, and civic leaders.
  • Strengthening the university’s presence across Africa and internationally.
  • Supporting the CEO’s office and Board in managing high-level stakeholder relationships.
  • Ensuring alignment between institutional messaging, partnerships, and mission.

Senior Leadership

  • Build and lead a high-performing Stakeholder Engagement department.
  • Establish clear strategies, goals, and metrics for fundraising, partnerships, and engagement.
  • Foster a culture of relationship stewardship, professionalism, and mission alignment.
  • Work closely with other executives to ensure stakeholder engagement supports institutional priorities.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

  • Significant leadership experience in fundraising, partnerships, external affairs, or stakeholder engagement.
  • A proven track record of building relationships that lead to funding, partnerships, or institutional growth.
  • Experience working with senior leaders, boards, donors, and global networks.
  • Familiarity with Africa’s development, philanthropic, or innovation ecosystems.
  • Experience in higher education is valuable but not required.

REQUIRED COMPETENCIES

  • Mission-Driven: Demonstrates deep personal alignment to Africa’s development and ALU’s mission, with the ability to inspire belief and mobilize diverse stakeholders (donors, partners, alumni, and communities) around a shared purpose.
  • Strategic: Builds and sustains trust-based, high-value relationships across sectors, cultures, and geographies, with strong judgment on how to engage, influence, and steward stakeholders over time.
  • Ownership & Excellence: Operates with a high level of accountability, translating ambitious ideas into tangible outcomes in a fast-moving, evolving environment, while maintaining quality and follow-through.
  • Systems Thinking: Sees connections across functions (fundraising, partnerships, brand, alumni, impact) and integrates them into a cohesive strategy, avoiding silos and maximizing institutional leverage.

Core Competencies

  • Proven ability to design and execute fundraising strategies, including major gifts, institutional funding, and partnership-linked revenue generation.
  • Expertise in shaping institutional narrative across marketing, PR, and impact reporting, translating outcomes into compelling stories that attract funding, partnerships, and influence.
  • Ability to originate, negotiate, and structure strategic partnerships that deliver mutual value across corporate, foundation, government, and ecosystem players.
  • Experience building and activating networks (alumni, communities, supporters) into engaged ecosystems that contribute to institutional growth, reputation, and impact.

jobs.title: Product Lead, Platform & Enterprise -Sureel AI
jobs.excerpt: A little bit about our team Sureel AI is building the standards and infrastructure for AI rights, licensing, attribution, protection, and intelligence, starting in music and expanding across media.
jobs.description:
A little bit about our team

Sureel AI is building the standards and infrastructure for AI rights, licensing, attribution, protection, and intelligence, starting in music and expanding across media.

We are building the infrastructure that enables creators and rightsholders to control how their work is used by AI, protect their rights, understand its use and value, and participate in new AI licensing models. At the same time, we provide AI companies and digital platforms with the systems required to access rights, permissions, attribution, guardrails, reporting, and licensing infrastructure programmatically.

Acquired by Warner Music Group, Sureel operates as an independent, federated company combining startup speed with the reach of a global music company.

We are now looking for a senior, highly hands-on product leader to turn our technology, commercial strategy, partner requirements, and industry vision into a coherent enterprise platform.

Your role

You will own the product direction and execution of the full Sureel stack, working closely with leadership, Engineering, AI, Business Development & Licensing, Client Relations, and our partners.

This is a hands-on product leadership role.

You will set product strategy and priorities, but you will also personally conduct customer discovery, talk to clients, research the market, write product requirements, map workflows, review designs, analyze usage, test products, work directly with engineers, and drive capabilities from concept through adoption.

You will help answer the core product questions that determine Sureel's future:

  • What should we build?
  • What should we not build?
  • What needs to become scalable platform infrastructure?
  • What should remain configurable or customer-specific?
  • What do enterprises need in order to deploy Sureel at scale?
  • How should commercial and licensing models translate into actual product workflows?
  • How do we turn partner feedback into a coherent product rather than a collection of bespoke features?

You will operate as the bridge between business strategy, customer needs, technology, and execution, ensuring Sureel builds products that customers adopt, use, and rely on.

Here you'll get to

    • Own product strategy and roadmap across the full Sureel stack, translating company goals, commercial opportunities, customer needs, and technical capabilities into clear priorities.
    • Be deeply involved with customers and partners, including labels, publishers, PROs/CMOs, artists, AI companies, DSPs, and other industry participants, to understand their workflows, problems, requirements, and priorities firsthand.
    • Lead continuous product discovery, including customer interviews, market research, competitive research, workflow analysis, prototype testing, and structured feedback gathering.
    • Turn commercial and licensing concepts into scalable product capabilities, working closely with Business Development & Licensing to ensure new deal structures can be executed through Sureel's technology.
    • Build enterprise-grade products, thinking beyond individual features into administration, permissions, roles, bulk workflows, APIs, integrations, auditability, reporting, configurability, security, reliability, and operational scalability.
    • Define what becomes core platform infrastructure, what should be configurable, what requires an integration, and what should remain a bespoke exception.
    • Write and own product requirements, including PRDs, user journeys, workflows, success metrics, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and implementation priorities.
    • Work directly with Engineering and AI teams throughout development, answering product questions, resolving trade-offs, removing ambiguity, testing functionality, and ensuring the shipped product solves the intended problem.
    • Partner closely with Client Relations to understand onboarding friction, adoption barriers, partner feedback, and opportunities to deepen usage across the platform.
    • Analyze product usage and partner behavior to understand what is working, where customers struggle, and where additional investment can create the greatest value.
    • Drive products through the entire lifecycle, from research and concept definition through development, launch, adoption, iteration, and expansion.
    • Establish product discipline and governance, including roadmap reviews, prioritization frameworks, product principles, decision-making processes, and clear mechanisms for evaluating new requests.
    • Define measurable outcomes for product investments, focusing on adoption, activation, customer value, commercial impact, operational efficiency, technical performance, and strategic importance rather than simply features shipped.
    • Identify patterns across customer requests and market developments, distinguishing individual requests from broader signals that should shape Sureel's platform or industry strategy.
    • Ensure Sureel's product architecture can support emerging industry frameworks and standards, so rights, licensing, permissions, attribution, and reporting can increasingly be executed programmatically.
    • Create clarity across teams, ensuring leadership, Engineering, AI, Commercial, Client Relations, and Marketing understand what we are building, why we are building it, and how success will be measured.
    • Help shape the future product organization as Sureel grows, including identifying where additional product, design, research, or operational resources are required.

What success looks like:

    You will help Sureel evolve from a collection of individual capabilities into a coherent enterprise platform.

    Success means:

    • Customers can understand and adopt the Sureel platform.
    • Enterprise partners can onboard and operate at scale.
    • Commercial agreements translate into repeatable product workflows.
    • Product priorities reflect customer value and company strategy.
    • Partner requests are evaluated consistently rather than driving reactive development.
    • Engineering receives clear, validated requirements.
    • Customer discovery continuously informs the roadmap.
    • Manual workflows become scalable product capabilities.
    • Product investments have measurable outcomes.
    • Product adoption grows across existing partner relationships.
    • Sureel has a clear product strategy, roadmap, and operating discipline.

Who you are:

    • You are an experienced product leader who has built enterprise B2B software, platforms, infrastructure, APIs, or technically complex products.
    • You have strong product judgment and remain deeply hands-on. You can set strategy, interview a customer, write requirements, review a workflow, and test a product yourself.
    • You have personally owned products from discovery through launch and adoption.
    • You are strong at customer discovery and know how to uncover the underlying problem rather than simply accepting a feature request.
    • You know how to translate complex business models, workflows, and customer requirements into scalable product systems.
    • You are comfortable working with technical teams and discussing APIs, data models, integrations, AI systems, infrastructure, and technical trade-offs.
    • You understand enterprise product requirements and how they differ from consumer products.
    • You are commercially minded and understand how product decisions connect to customer value, adoption, strategic advantage, and business outcomes.
    • You know how to distinguish between solving one customer's problem and building a capability that belongs in the platform.
    • You are comfortable operating with incomplete information and creating structure in a fast-changing category.
    • You communicate clearly across technical, commercial, customer, and executive audiences.
    • You enjoy working in a small startup where product leadership means doing the work yourself.

We’d love it if you also had:

    • Experience building products in media, music, rights management, licensing, payments, marketplaces, compliance, or creator platforms.
    • Experience with multi-sided platforms or ecosystems involving different stakeholder groups.
    • Experience building products for large enterprises with complex organizational structures and workflows.
    • Experience with AI or machine-learning products, APIs, developer infrastructure, or data-intensive platforms.
    • Experience translating contracts, pricing models, or business rules into product capabilities.
    • Experience as an early product hire or product leader who helped build product practices from scratch.
    • Experience working directly with C-level executives and translating company strategy into product execution.
    • Curiosity about the intersection of AI, technology, intellectual property, and the creative industries.

Sureel AI is an independent, federated company within Warner Music Group. We're committed to building a diverse team and to fair recognition and compensation for creators everywhere.
