jobs.title: Software Engineer III
jobs.excerpt: About Renaissance When you join Renaissance®, you join a global leader in pre-K–12 education technology!
jobs.description:
About Renaissance

When you join Renaissance®, you join a global leader in pre-K–12 education technology! Renaissance’s solutions help educators analyze, customize, and plan personalized learning paths for students, allowing time for what matters—creating energizing learning experiences in the classroom. Our fiercely passionate employees and educational partners have helped drive phenomenal student growth, with Renaissance solutions being used in over one-third of US schools and in more than 100 countries worldwide.

Every day, we are connected to our mission by exemplifying our values: trust each other, win together, strive for the best, own our actions, and grow and evolve.

Job Description

As a Software Engineer III, you will build features across the discovery layer and the products behind it: the search and browse experiences teachers use to find the right lesson, the curation tools admins use to govern what their district sees, and the services that make four separate products feel like one library. You will be making it fast and intuitive for admins to govern and curate, for teachers to find and instruct, and for students to explore and grow their respective libraries. You will work with a high degree of independence and help ensure that problems and solutions are appropriately scoped.

In addition, you will be the first team to adopt Renaissance’s S3 model of software development. You will be expected to build multi-agent orchestration, where specialized agents coordinate on complete features and engineers shift from managing individual tasks to designing the systems that produce the work.

In this role as a Software Engineer III, you will: 

  • Build features across the discovery layer and the products it connects — search and browse for teachers, curation and governance for admins, exploration for students.
  • Develop backend services that leverage relational databases, non-relational datastores, message queuing, and cloud infrastructure, against typed contracts.
  • Build and test frontend experiences in TypeScript and React, contract-tested against the backend, with accessibility treated as a requirement rather than a follow-up.
  • Write the tests and the instrumentation with the feature — unit, component, and contract tests, plus the traces, metrics, and logs that make the system debuggable.

Qualifications

For this role, you must have: 

  • Professional experience building and shipping production web applications or services.
  • Experience developing backend services against relational databases, and comfort with non-relational datastores, message queuing, and/or cloud infrastructure.
  • Excitement to help craft a new, AI-first software development lifecycle. The idea of encoding engineering understanding into formal constraints that can be consumed by an AI workflow is an interesting problem to you, not a necessary evil.
  • Working knowledge of cloud operations — you can deploy across environments, read a dashboard, and troubleshoot an application problem in a cloud environment.
  • Effective communication skills and the ability to collaborate well with distributed engineering, product, and design teams.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent industry experience.

Experience with various engineering technologies such as: 

  • SQL (MSSQL, PostgreSQL, etc.)
  • Proficiency in a typed language, ideally TypeScript, and comfort working in a strictly typed codebase.

  Optionally, you could have: 

  • Experience leading and mentoring others 
  • Experience with the AWS technologies
  • Knowledge of DevOps processes and technologies

Additional information

We’re looking for a senior QA engineer who sees quality as a property of the whole system, not a phase at the end. You’ll work with our QA lead to shape how quality works across the project. You’ll also stay hands-on: writing automation, building tools, and working directly with delivery teams.

  • Define and evolve the quality strategy for the whole project together with the QA lead.

  • Find process and team bottlenecks, then build or suggest tooling and practices that remove them.

  • Make sure our tests are meaningful: the right tests at the right level, giving reliable signal, rather than just raising coverage numbers.

  • Design, build, and maintain automated tests and test tooling using open-source tools.

  • Support delivery teams in their quality practices, and use your testing experience to push for testable design and good engineering habits.

  • Explore how AI tools can help, and where they can hurt, in testing, triage, and release work.

  • Test hands-on: whether with your tools or with your inquisitive nature doing some manual testing, too.

What you bring

  • Several years of experience in software quality, including leading or shaping quality processes beyond executing tests

  • Proactivity: you spot problems and act on them without waiting to be told

  • Solid scripting and automation skills in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Java

  • Experience testing web applications and APIs

  • Comfort with CI/CD pipelines and the tooling around them

  • The user focus: you’re not afraid to do some manual testing yourself and dig deeper into user workflows, so the automation that's done is also automating the right things.

  • Strong communication skills: you can advocate for quality with developers, product people and managers, and win them over without becoming a gatekeeper

Nice to have

  • Experience with open-source projects or distributed teams

  • Experience with Java/Spring, React, or Android

  • Experience with performance testing, multi-version support, or data-heavy systems

  • Interest in global health or digital public goods

Location and Employment Details
Remote (Central European Time Zone +/- 2 hours). This is a full-time position on a 1-year renewable contract.

Cover letter
We appreciate candidates providing a short (human :)) cover letter about their specific interest in DHIS2 and the role.

We are a well-funded not-for-profit project tasked with building the open-source DHIS2 platform, the world’s most widely deployed health information system. The project is based at the HISP Centre at the University of Oslo (UiO), where we operate as an independent software development organization.

With us, you get a chance to work on problems that really matter: Improving the health and well-being of people around the world through access to and use of information. Our platform is used in more than 90 countries worldwide and has the scale and adoption that will allow you to make an impact globally.

At DHIS2, we believe you will do your best work if you fully understand the context in which the system operates. As a result, we encourage you to engage directly with our projects, take part in the design process, and get feedback from users in the field.

jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.
